question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Plants of a particular region
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Flora.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Flora refers to the plants of a particular region, period, or environment taken as a whole. (किसी क्षेत्र के पौधे/वनस्पति)
◦ Example: The flora of the Himalayan region includes rhododendrons, pines and alpine meadows.

• The word is borrowed from Latin Flora, the Roman goddess of flowers and spring.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Flinch — to draw back or wince suddenly, usually from pain, fear, or a difficult situation; not related to plants.

• Option 3: Fauna — refers to the animals of a particular region or period, as opposed to its plants. (किसी क्षेत्र के प्राणी)

• Option 4: Flotsam — wreckage or debris found floating on the sea, or discarded odds and ends.

NOTE

• Flora and fauna is a fixed pair used together to mean the plant and animal life of a region.

• Similar one-word substitutes: Flock (a group of birds/sheep), Herbivore (a plant-eating animal), Habitat (the natural home of a plant or animal).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Abu said that he saw the picture.
option_2: he will have seen the picture
option_3: he would have seen the picture
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. he had seen the picture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Abu said that he saw the picture" is a case of Narration (Direct-Indirect Speech) where the reporting verb "said" is in the Past Tense.

• Rule — Backshift of tenses in Indirect Speech: When the reporting verb is in the past tense, the tense of the reported speech also shifts backward (backshift). The Simple Past (saw) in the reported clause changes to the Past Perfect (had seen).
◦ Direct: He said, "I saw the picture."
◦ Indirect: He said that he had seen the picture.

• Applying the rule, the underlined segment "he saw the picture" must be changed to "he had seen the picture".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "he has seen the picture" is incorrect because the Present Perfect Tense cannot be used to backshift a Simple Past clause when the reporting verb is in the past.

• Option 2: "he will have seen the picture" is incorrect because the Future Perfect Tense has no logical basis here; nothing in the sentence indicates a future reference point.

• Option 3: "he would have seen the picture" is incorrect because "would have" expresses an unfulfilled past condition/possibility, not a simple backshift of the Simple Past tense.

NOTE

• Common tense backshifts in narration: Simple Present → Simple Past; Simple Past → Past Perfect; Present Continuous → Past Continuous; Present Perfect → Past Perfect.

• If the reported statement expresses a universal truth or habitual fact, the tense usually remains unchanged even after a past reporting verb.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Slege.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Siege" — a military operation in which an army surrounds and blockades a town or fortress to force its surrender.
◦ Example: The city was under siege for nearly a year before it finally surrendered.

• Spelling key: S + IE + G + E. Remember the rule "i before e except after c" — since there is no "c" before it, the sequence is "ie", not "ei".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Texture" is correctly spelt — the surface feel or appearance of a material.

• Option 3: "Savoury" is correctly spelt — having a pleasant taste or smell, typically salty or spicy rather than sweet.

• Option 4: "Tamper" is correctly spelt — to interfere with something without authority.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused "ie/ei" words: believe, achieve, receive, ceiling, ancient, weird.

• Related words to "siege": besiege, beleaguer.

question:
Select the appropriate adverb for the underlined word in the sentence.
He led me to the room that had obvious been built later than the rest of the house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. obviously.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "He led me to the room that had obvious been built later than the rest of the house" requires a word that modifies the verb phrase "had... been built".

• Rule — Adverbs modify verbs: An adverb, not an adjective, is used to modify a verb, another adverb, or an adjective. Since "obvious" is being used to modify the passive verb "had been built", it must be changed to its adverb form "obviously" (formed by adding -ly to the adjective).

• Corrected sentence: He led me to the room that had obviously been built later than the rest of the house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "oblivously" is not a standard English word at all; it appears to be a misspelling and has no valid meaning here.

• Option 2: "obliviousness" is a noun meaning "the state of being unaware", which does not fit the sentence structure as it cannot modify a verb.

• Option 3: "obviousness" is also a noun (meaning "the quality of being obvious") and grammatically cannot function as an adverb modifying the verb.

NOTE

• Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding -ly to the adjective: clear → clearly, quick → quickly, careful → carefully.

• Do not confuse the adjective (obvious), the adverb (obviously), and the noun (obviousness) — only the adverb form can modify a verb.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A shortened version of a larger work
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Abridgement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An Abridgement is a shortened version of a book or other piece of writing that keeps the main content/story but removes some of the length. (किसी बड़ी रचना का संक्षिप्त रूप)
◦ Example: This children's edition is an abridgement of the original 900-page novel.

• The verb form is "abridge", meaning to shorten a piece of writing without losing its essential content.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Summary (सारांश) — a brief statement of the main points of something, generally written in one's own words; it need not preserve the structure of the original larger work.

• Option 2: Précis (संक्षेप) — a concise summary of the essential points of a text, focused on brevity of ideas rather than being a "shortened version" of the full original work.

• Option 3: Shorts — informal, refers to short trousers or short films; unrelated to written works.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Anthology (a collection of poems/writings), Compendium (a collection of concise but detailed information), Digest (a summarized collection of material).

• Do not confuse abridge (to shorten) with abrogate (to formally abolish/repeal, as a law).

question:
Complete the following collocation.
I was running late so I only had time for a _______ shower.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. quick.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A collocation is a natural, fixed pairing of words that native speakers habitually use together, even when other words with a similar meaning would also make grammatical sense.

• In English, the fixed collocation for a brief wash is "a quick shower" (or "a quick bath"), used to describe something done rapidly due to lack of time.
◦ Example: I had a quick shower before leaving for work.

• Applying this, the blank in **"I only had time for a ___ shower" must be filled with "quick"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "hasty" usually collocates with words like "decision", "retreat", or "conclusion", not with "shower"; it also carries a negative connotation of being rash.

• Option 3: "fast" is grammatically an adjective/adverb of speed but does not collocate naturally with "shower" in standard English usage.

• Option 4: "short" describes duration/length rather than speed, and "a short shower" is far less idiomatic than "a quick shower" in this context.

NOTE

• Other fixed collocations with "quick": quick glance, quick nap, quick meal, quick decision.

• Collocation questions cannot be solved by grammar rules alone — they must be learned as fixed word-pairs through reading and practice.

question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
Her phone can't be switched off by my father.
option_1: My father switches off her phone.
option_2: My father could not switch off her phone.
option_3: My father have not switched off her phone.
option_4: My father can't switch off her phone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. My father can't switch off her phone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Her phone can't be switched off by my father" is in the Passive Voice with the modal auxiliary "can" (negative form "can't").

• Rule — Passive to Active with Modal Verbs:
◦ Passive: Object + modal + be + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + modal + V1 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "by my father" becomes the subject "My father"; the modal "can't" stays unchanged; the past participle "switched off" reverts to the base form "switch off"; and the passive subject "Her phone" becomes the object.
◦ Active: My father can't switch off her phone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "My father switches off her phone" is incorrect because it drops the modal "can't" entirely and changes the meaning to a Simple Present statement.

• Option 2: "My father could not switch off her phone" is incorrect because it changes the modal from "can't" (present ability/permission) to "could not" (past tense), altering the tense of the sentence.

• Option 3: "My father have not switched off her phone" is incorrect because it is grammatically wrong (subject-verb agreement: "has not", not "have not") and also wrongly converts the sentence into the Present Perfect tense instead of retaining the modal "can't".

NOTE

• Modals such as can, could, may, might, must, will, would, shall, should remain the same when converting between active and passive voice — only the verb after the modal changes form (V1 in active, V3 in passive).

• The negative particle "not" (or its contraction) always stays attached to the modal in both voices.

question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
Shyam asked me how I had persuaded his sister.
option_1: "How are you persuading my sister?" Shyam asked me.
option_2: "How did you persuaded my sister?" Shyam asked me.
option_3: "How did you persuade my sister?" Shyam asked me.
option_4: "How have you persuade my sister?" Shyam asks me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. "How did you persuade my sister?" Shyam asked me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Shyam asked me how I had persuaded his sister" is in Indirect Speech, with the reported verb in the Past Perfect Tense (had persuaded).

• Rule — Indirect to Direct Speech (Past Perfect → Simple Past in a question): When a past perfect tense in indirect speech is converted back to direct speech, it becomes the Simple Past Tense, and for a question, the auxiliary "did" is used along with the base form of the verb, and the sentence is framed as a direct question with a question mark.
◦ Pronoun changes: "me" → "you", "his sister" → "my sister" (since Shyam is now speaking directly).
◦ Interrogative word "how" is retained at the start of the direct question.

• Applying the rule: "how I had persuaded his sister" becomes "How did you persuade my sister?", framed as Shyam's own direct question.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "How are you persuading my sister?" is incorrect because it wrongly uses the Present Continuous Tense instead of the Simple Past.

• Option 2: "How did you persuaded my sister?" is incorrect because after the auxiliary "did", the main verb must be in its base form (persuade), not the past form (persuaded).

• Option 4: "How have you persuade my sister?" is incorrect on two counts — it uses the wrong tense (Present Perfect: "have...persuade" is not even correctly formed, which would need "persuaded"), and the reporting verb is wrongly changed to present tense "asks" instead of the required past tense "asked".

NOTE

• When converting indirect questions back to direct speech, restore the interrogative word order (auxiliary before subject) and the question mark.

• Backshift reversal chart: Past Perfect (indirect) → Simple Past (direct); Present Perfect (indirect) → Simple Present (direct); Past Continuous (indirect) → Present Continuous (direct).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The interviewees were slowly becoming impatient as they were left to ________ in the waiting room for hours.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cool their heels.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to cool one's heels" means to be kept waiting for a long time, especially due to someone else's delay. (लंबे समय तक इंतजार करना)
◦ Example: The candidates had to cool their heels outside the interview room for over an hour.

• In the given sentence, the interviewees becoming impatient while waiting in the waiting room for hours perfectly matches this idiom's meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To draw the long bow (बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर बात करना): To exaggerate or stretch the truth.

• Option 3: To hold water (तर्कसंगत होना): To be valid, sound, or logical (usually used of an argument or theory).

• Option 4: To flog a dead horse (व्यर्थ प्रयास करना): To waste effort trying to revive interest in a matter that is already settled or hopeless.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to waiting: "To be kept on tenterhooks" (to be kept in anxious suspense), "To wait with bated breath" (to wait anxiously/excitedly).

• Do not confuse "cool one's heels" (wait) with "kick up one's heels" (to celebrate/have fun).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
One can never imagine / how hot it gets in Delhi / unless one doesn't go / there in person.
option_3: how hot it gets in Delhi
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. unless one doesn't go.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The conjunction "unless" already carries a negative meaning — it means "if not" or "except if".

• Rule — Unless is never used with another negative (no double negatives): Since "unless" itself functions as a negative conditional, the clause that follows it must be in the affirmative (positive) form, not the negative form.
◦ Incorrect: unless one doesn't go
◦ Correct: unless one goes

• Applying the rule, the segment "unless one doesn't go" wrongly repeats the negative idea (since "unless" = "if...not"), producing a double negative that reverses the intended meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "One can never imagine" is grammatically correct; "never" here correctly negates the main clause.

• Option 3: "how hot it gets in Delhi" is grammatically correct — a properly formed noun clause acting as the object of "imagine".

• Option 4: "there in person" is grammatically correct and simply completes the sentence.

NOTE

• Other words that already carry a built-in negative sense and must NOT be paired with "not" or another negative word: hardly, scarcely, barely, seldom, few, little, without.
◦ Example: She could hardly walk (NOT "She could hardly not walk" / "She couldn't hardly walk").

• "Unless" is commonly tested in error-spotting and fill-in-the-blank questions for this exact double-negative trap.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'MOBILE' from the given sentence.
The strange TV reporter standing over there covers all the funny and interesting things happening inside the town.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Standing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mobile means capable of moving or being moved freely or easily; not fixed in one place. (गतिशील / चल)

• Its antonym is a word meaning fixed or unable to move — "Standing" here is used in the sense of stationary/stationed in one place, which is the opposite of being mobile.
◦ Example: The mobile clinic can reach remote villages, unlike the standing hospital building.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Interesting — means engaging or attention-grabbing; unrelated in meaning to "mobile".

• Option 3: Inside — a preposition/adverb of location; not an antonym of "mobile".

• Option 4: Strange — means unusual or unfamiliar; unrelated in meaning to "mobile".

NOTE

• Other common antonyms of "mobile": immobile, stationary, fixed, static, motionless.

• Do not confuse "mobile" (able to move) with "movable" (able to be moved by someone) — in most SSC contexts they are treated as close synonyms, but "mobile" more often describes self-directed movement (e.g., "a mobile phone" = it moves with you).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Exaltation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ecstasy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Exaltation means a feeling of intense happiness, elation, or triumphant joy. (अत्यधिक हर्ष / उल्लास)
◦ Example: A sense of exaltation filled the climbers as they reached the summit.

• Ecstasy means an overwhelming feeling of great happiness or joyful excitement, which closely matches the meaning of "exaltation".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Dejection (निराशा) — a state of sadness or low spirits; this is actually closer to an antonym of "exaltation".

• Option 3: Satisfaction (संतुष्टि) — a feeling of contentment, which is milder than the intense joy conveyed by "exaltation".

• Option 4: Elaboration (विस्तार) — the act of adding further detail or explanation; unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of exaltation: elation, euphoria, rapture, jubilation.

• Do not confuse exaltation (great joy/elevation) with exhalation (breathing out) — they are commonly confused due to similar spelling.

question:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. Main source of water for Wular Lake is River Jhelum.
Q. Wular Lake is also said to be a remnant of Satisar Lake that existed in ancient times.
R. This lake also has a small island in its centre called the 'Zaina Lank'.
S. This island was constructed by King Zainul-Abi-Din.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PRSQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a paragraph/sentence-ordering (para jumble) question, the correct order is found by identifying the topic sentence (the one that introduces the subject in the most general way) and then tracing the logical/pronoun-based links between the remaining sentences.

• P is the ideal opening sentence as it introduces the main subject, Wular Lake, and its most basic fact — its main source of water (River Jhelum).

• R follows P naturally, using "This lake" to refer back to Wular Lake already introduced in P, and adds a further fact — the presence of a small island, 'Zaina Lank'.

• S follows R because it uses "This island", directly referring to the island named in R, and gives more detail about who constructed it.

• Q comes last, rounding off the paragraph with an additional historical fact about the lake's ancient origin (as a remnant of Satisar Lake).

• Applying these pronoun and logical links gives the order: P → R → S → Q.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: RPQS is incorrect because it opens with "This lake" (R), but the pronoun "This" needs an antecedent that has not yet been introduced, making it an illogical opening.

• Option 2: PQRS disrupts the close link between R ("This lake also has a small island") and S ("This island was constructed..."), placing Q in between and breaking the pronoun reference chain.

• Option 3: QSRP is incorrect because it opens with Q, which refers to "Wular Lake" as if already known, and it separates R from S, breaking the "This island" reference.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always scan for pronouns (this, that, it, these, those) and linking words (also, however, therefore) — they are the strongest clues to identify which sentence must directly follow another.

• The sentence introducing the subject by its full name (not a pronoun) is almost always the opening sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Oppose
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Encourage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Oppose means to disagree with or resist something/someone; to actively work against. (विरोध करना)

• Encourage means to support, promote, or give confidence to someone/something, which is the direct opposite of opposing something.
◦ Example: Instead of opposing his plan, the board decided to encourage it with additional funding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Embody (मूर्त रूप देना) — to represent or express an idea/quality in a tangible form; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 2: Resist (प्रतिरोध करना) — to withstand or fight against something; this is actually a synonym, not an antonym, of "oppose".

• Option 4: Elective — chosen by election, or (as an adjective) optional; unrelated in meaning to "oppose".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "oppose": resist, object to, contest, combat.

• Other antonyms of "oppose": support, favour, back, endorse, advocate.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Technology plays an indispensable role in the lives of human beings in the 21st century.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Superfluous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indispensable means absolutely necessary or essential; something that cannot be done without. (अनिवार्य / अपरिहार्य)

• Superfluous means more than what is needed; unnecessary or excessive, which is the direct opposite of being essential.
◦ Example: Once the main point was made, the extra examples felt superfluous.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Relentless (अथक) — unceasingly intense or persistent; unrelated in meaning to "indispensable".

• Option 3: Vigilant (सतर्क) — keeping careful watch for possible danger; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: Unprecedented (अभूतपूर्व) — never done or known before; unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "indispensable": essential, vital, crucial, necessary.

• Other antonyms of "indispensable": dispensable, unnecessary, unimportant, redundant.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word. Choose the correct alternative.
When there are negative and toxic thoughts _______ your mind, you can never think positively.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. clouding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence requires a verb that describes negative and toxic thoughts affecting one's ability to think clearly.

• "To cloud one's mind" is the standard collocation/expression meaning to confuse or obscure someone's clear thinking or judgment.
◦ Example: Anger clouded his judgment, and he made a hasty decision.

• Applying this to the sentence: "When there are negative and toxic thoughts clouding your mind, you can never think positively" fits both the grammar and the intended meaning perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "plotting" means secretly planning something, usually a scheme; it does not fit the context of thoughts affecting one's mind.

• Option 2: "shouting" means speaking very loudly; it cannot logically apply to "thoughts" in this context.

• Option 4: "persuading" means convincing someone to do or believe something; thoughts cannot "persuade" a mind in this idiomatic sense — it does not fit the fixed expression being tested.

NOTE

• Other similar fixed expressions with "mind": to cross one's mind (to occur to someone), to make up one's mind (to decide), to have something on one's mind (to be worried about something), to slip one's mind (to forget).

• Choosing the correct word in cloze/fill-in-the-blank questions often depends on knowing which verb naturally collocates with the noun in context, not just individual word meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Break the ice
option_1: Make people meeting first time feel uncomfortable
option_2: Make people meeting first time feel sad
option_3: Make people meeting first time feel more detached
option_4: Make people meeting first time feel more comfortable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Make people meeting first time feel more comfortable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Break the ice" means to do or say something that relieves tension or awkwardness, especially at the start of a conversation between people meeting for the first time, making them feel more relaxed and comfortable. (अजनबियों के बीच की झिझक को दूर करना)
◦ Example: The host told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.

• The idiom originates from the practice of ships called "icebreakers" that cut through frozen ice to allow other ships to pass — figuratively, "breaking the ice" clears the way for smoother interaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Make people meeting first time feel uncomfortable" is the opposite of the idiom's actual meaning.

• Option 2: "Make people meeting first time feel sad" does not relate to the idiom's meaning of easing social tension.

• Option 3: "Make people meeting first time feel more detached" is also opposite in spirit — the idiom is about creating connection, not distance.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to social interaction: "Hit it off" (to get along well with someone immediately), "Get off on the right foot" (to start a relationship or task well), "Rub someone the wrong way" (to irritate someone).

• Do not confuse "break the ice" with "cut no ice" (to have no influence or effect on someone).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The wounded man was being helped by a few men.
option_1: The wounded man had been helped by a few men.
option_2: A few men were helping the wounded man.
option_3: The wounded man was helping a few men.
option_4: A few men are helping the wounded man.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A few men were helping the wounded man.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The wounded man was being helped by a few men" is in the Passive Voice, Past Continuous Tense.

• Rule — Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule in reverse: the agent "a few men" becomes the subject; since it is plural, the auxiliary is "were"; the past participle "helped" changes to the present participle "helping"; and "the wounded man" (the passive subject) becomes the object.
◦ Active: A few men were helping the wounded man.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "The wounded man had been helped by a few men" is incorrect because it changes the tense to the Past Perfect passive, which does not correspond to the original Past Continuous passive sentence, and it is also still in the passive voice, not active.

• Option 3: "The wounded man was helping a few men" is incorrect because it wrongly interchanges the subject and object, reversing the meaning (making the wounded man the one who helps, rather than the one being helped).

• Option 4: "A few men are helping the wounded man" is incorrect because it uses the Present Continuous Tense ("are helping") instead of the required Past Continuous Tense ("were helping").

NOTE

• When converting Continuous Tense passives to active voice, remember that "being" (in passive) has no separate counterpart in active voice — it disappears, and the main verb takes the "-ing" form directly after the auxiliary.

• Tense must always be preserved exactly when converting between active and passive voice — only the subject/object and verb form change.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mortifeid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Mortified" — feeling very embarrassed or humiliated.
◦ Example: She was mortified when she realised she had called her teacher "Mum" by mistake.

• Spelling key: MORTI + FIED. The correct sequence is "i" before "e" — "-ified", not "-ifeid". The base word is "mortify" (to embarrass deeply), and the "-y" changes to "-i" before adding "-fied" in the past tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Benign" is correctly spelt — gentle, kindly, or (in medical use) not harmful/cancerous.

• Option 3: "Insecurities" is correctly spelt — the plural of "insecurity", a feeling of uncertainty or lack of confidence.

• Option 4: "Dismay" is correctly spelt — a feeling of concern, disappointment, or distress.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-ify" typically form their past tense by changing "y" to "i" and adding "-ed": mortify → mortified, terrify → terrified, classify → classified.

• Other commonly misspelt words with similar "ie/ei" traps: receive, believe, achieve, deceive.

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
The continued
P. the growing sales of sneakers
Q. dominance of the athleisure trend
R. along with the pursuit of comfort
S. has had a significant impact on
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. QSPR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed opening "The continued" is an adjective phrase that must be immediately followed by a noun it modifies — "dominance" — so the sentence must begin with Q ("dominance of the athleisure trend").

• After establishing the subject "The continued dominance of the athleisure trend", the verb phrase S ("has had a significant impact on") must follow to complete the main clause (Subject + Verb).

• The verb phrase then requires its object, which is P ("the growing sales of sneakers"), followed by the final modifying phrase R ("along with the pursuit of comfort"), which adds an additional related cause.

• Applying this order gives the coherent sentence: "The continued dominance of the athleisure trend has had a significant impact on the growing sales of sneakers, along with the pursuit of comfort."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: PSRQ is incorrect because it places the object (P) immediately after "The continued", which does not grammatically or logically follow, since "continued" needs a noun like "dominance" to modify first.

• Option 2: RPSQ is incorrect because it opens with a subordinate phrase (R) right after "The continued", leaving the sentence without a proper subject at the start.

• Option 3: QRPS is incorrect because it inserts R ("along with the pursuit of comfort") between the subject (Q) and the main verb (S), breaking the Subject-Verb continuity of the sentence.

NOTE

• In sentence-rearrangement questions, always locate the main Subject and main Verb first — they typically anchor the rest of the sentence around them.

• Phrases beginning with "along with", "as well as", or "in addition to" usually function as trailing modifiers and are placed toward the end of a sentence, not at its start.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly (1)_________. Individual coping qualities (2)_________ the behaviour of stressful drivers. Instead of being enraged over circumstances beyond their control, drivers (3)_________ learn to be patient. On the road, we must be (4)_________ to control our own emotions. Road raged drivers are also more likely to (5)_________ more traffic offences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. involved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the linking verb "are" in the clause **"whether they are directly or indirectly ________", which requires a word that can function as a complement/adjective** after "are".

• "Involved" is the past participle of the verb "involve", commonly used as an adjective meaning connected with or taking part in something. It fits naturally after "are" to describe drivers being "directly or indirectly involved" in road rage incidents.

• Applying this, the completed sentence reads: "All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly involved."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "involves" is the third-person singular present form of the verb and cannot follow "are" in this construction — it would require a different sentence structure such as "it involves them".

• Option 2: "involving" is the present participle/gerund form; while participles can sometimes follow "be" verbs, "are...involving" would need an object and does not fit the intended passive/adjectival sense here.

• Option 4: "involve" is the base form of the verb, which cannot directly follow "are" as a complement in this construction (it would need "to involve" or a different subject-verb agreement pattern).

NOTE

• After forms of "be" (is/am/are/was/were), a past participle (V3) commonly functions as an adjective describing a state, e.g., "interested", "involved", "concerned", "affected" — this is a frequently tested pattern in SSC cloze passages.

• Do not confuse the passive/adjectival past participle ("involved") with the active present participle ("involving"), which would need a following object.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly (1)_________. Individual coping qualities (2)_________ the behaviour of stressful drivers. Instead of being enraged over circumstances beyond their control, drivers (3)_________ learn to be patient. On the road, we must be (4)_________ to control our own emotions. Road raged drivers are also more likely to (5)_________ more traffic offences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. influence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "Individual coping qualities", which is a plural noun phrase, and the sentence is in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement in Simple Present Tense: With a plural subject, the main verb takes its base form (without "-s"), e.g., "qualities influence", not "qualities influences".

• Among the options, "influence" is both grammatically correct (base form, agreeing with the plural subject) and semantically appropriate, since "coping qualities" can logically influence (affect or shape) a driver's behaviour.
◦ Completed sentence: "Individual coping qualities influence the behaviour of stressful drivers."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "apply" does not fit the intended meaning here — "qualities apply the behaviour" is not idiomatic English; "apply" needs a different object structure (e.g., "apply to").

• Option 3: "increases" is grammatically wrong (singular verb form with a plural subject) and also does not fit the meaning of the sentence.

• Option 4: "multiply" does not fit the meaning — "coping qualities multiply the behaviour" does not make logical sense in this context.

NOTE

• Always check both (a) subject-verb agreement and (b) contextual meaning when solving cloze passage blanks — an option may be grammatically valid but semantically wrong, or vice versa.

• Plural subjects such as "qualities", "drivers", "people" always take the base form of the verb in the Simple Present Tense.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly (1)_________. Individual coping qualities (2)_________ the behaviour of stressful drivers. Instead of being enraged over circumstances beyond their control, drivers (3)_________ learn to be patient. On the road, we must be (4)_________ to control our own emotions. Road raged drivers are also more likely to (5)_________ more traffic offences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. must.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence **"drivers ________ learn to be patient" requires a modal auxiliary verb that is directly followed by the base form of the main verb "learn"**.

• "Must" is a modal verb expressing necessity or strong obligation, and it is always followed directly by the base form of the verb (must + V1), which fits both the grammar and the meaning ("drivers must learn to be patient" = it is necessary for drivers to learn patience).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "can" would grammatically fit the structure (can + V1) but changes the meaning to ability/possibility rather than the necessity implied by the passage's tone (advising drivers on proper conduct).

• Option 3: "ought" is grammatically incorrect here, as "ought" must always be followed by "to" before the base verb (ought to learn), not the bare verb directly.

• Option 4: "to" alone is a preposition/infinitive marker, not a modal verb, and cannot correctly fill this blank before "learn" without another modal such as "ought" preceding it.

NOTE

• Modal verbs (can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will, would) are always followed by the base form of the verb, with no "to" in between — except "ought to" and "have to", which are exceptions requiring "to".

• "Must" expresses strong necessity/obligation, while "should" and "ought to" express advice or moral obligation — a subtle distinction often tested in SSC grammar questions.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly (1)_________. Individual coping qualities (2)_________ the behaviour of stressful drivers. Instead of being enraged over circumstances beyond their control, drivers (3)_________ learn to be patient. On the road, we must be (4)_________ to control our own emotions. Road raged drivers are also more likely to (5)_________ more traffic offences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. able.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence **"we must be ________ to control our own emotions" requires a word that fits the fixed construction "be able to + verb"**, meaning to have the capacity or skill to do something.

• "Able" is the correct adjective to complete this construction: "must be able to control" means "must have the capacity to control".
◦ Example: Drivers must be able to control their emotions even in stressful traffic situations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "brave" does not fit the fixed expression "be ___ to" in the sense required here; "must be brave to control" changes the meaning to courage rather than capability, and is not the natural collocation used in this context.

• Option 2: "consistent" does not fit grammatically or contextually — "must be consistent to control our own emotions" is not idiomatic English.

• Option 4: "oblige" is a verb, not an adjective, and cannot correctly follow "be" in this construction (the correct related adjective form would be "obliged", which would also not fit the intended meaning of capability).

NOTE

• The fixed expression "be able to + base verb" is used to express capability or capacity, and is a very common structure tested in SSC cloze and error-spotting questions.

• Do not confuse "able" (capable) with "capable" (which is followed by "of + gerund": capable of controlling) — both express similar meaning but require different following structures.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

All drivers are affected by road rage, whether they are directly or indirectly (1)_________. Individual coping qualities (2)_________ the behaviour of stressful drivers. Instead of being enraged over circumstances beyond their control, drivers (3)_________ learn to be patient. On the road, we must be (4)_________ to control our own emotions. Road raged drivers are also more likely to (5)_________ more traffic offences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. incur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence **"Road raged drivers are also more likely to ________ more traffic offences" requires a verb meaning to become subject to or bring upon oneself (something usually undesirable, such as a penalty, loss, or offence)**.

• "Incur" precisely means to become liable to or experience something unpleasant as a result of one's own actions, which fits the context of road-raged drivers bringing traffic offences upon themselves through their reckless behaviour.
◦ Example: Reckless driving can cause a person to incur heavy fines and penalty points.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "drag" means to pull something along forcefully or (informally) to make something last longer than necessary; it does not fit the meaning of bringing an offence upon oneself.

• Option 2: "reflect" means to think deeply about something or to show/mirror something; it does not fit the context of committing or acquiring traffic offences.

• Option 4: "proceed" means to continue or go forward with an action; it does not carry the sense of "bringing upon oneself" required by the sentence.

NOTE

• "Incur" is commonly used with negative consequences: incur a loss, incur a debt, incur a penalty, incur someone's wrath/displeasure.

• Do not confuse "incur" (to bring upon oneself, usually something negative) with "occur" (to happen) or "ensure" (to make certain) — these are commonly confused in SSC vocabulary-based questions due to similar spelling patterns.
